title: CWE-287: unauthenticated, unlimited lead/contact writes (no auth, no rate limiting, no CSRF)
description: POST /api/leads/create (lead.py:10) accepts arbitrary JSON and persists a LeadDB row with zero authentication, no rate limiting, no CSRF protection, and no origin checks beyond CORS (which is browser-enforced and does not stop curl). Pydantic bounds (name 2-100, email format, phone 10-20) are trivially satisfied by an attacker. Impact: unlimited spam rows fill the SQLite DB (disk exhaustion over time), pollute PII tables used for sales follow-up, and the response 400/500 behavior can be probed freely as an oracle. The same applies to the calculator endpoint (stateless, lower impact) and the contact stub.
impact: DB abuse/spam (lead table fill, PII pollution, disk growth), abusable error oracle; no integrity or privacy protection on PII ingestion.
mitigation: Add authentication/authorization, per-IP and per-session rate limiting (e.g., slowapi or a proxy WAF), CSRF protection for state-changing endpoints, and input fingerprinting (honeypots, captcha).
